deviations: Q-033 (design working assumption: (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) is unique in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions): built on it. A repeated key fails usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription with error 2627 at staging (logged Failed, re-raised, bronze unchanged), rather than landing one of the rows arbitrarily. Unit test 'duplicate source key fails...' pins this down.
notes:
MOD-004 builds MIG-0006: brnz_corporate_subscription (PK on contact_no, scheme_no, sub_campaign_year; Round not landed), usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription, the seeded silv_ref_payer_type (0 Unknown, -1 Unrecognised, -2 Not applicable, 1 Individual, 2 Corporate, ids set explicitly; the down script deletes exactly these rows), dim_payer_type and usp_load_dim_payer_type (same pattern as usp_load_dim_payment_method). The tSQLt suite failed 0/23 before any objects existed and passes 23/23 now. 7 developer unit tests were added, so 30/30 pass. Round-trip and check pass. sqlfluff findings are advisory style points, left as they are to match the Phase 1 and MOD-002/003 code.
Bronze load: the source is first copied into a temp table with the same types as the target and the key NOT NULL. So a NULL Contact No, Scheme No or Sub Campaign Year fails the load with 515 before bronze is touched (answers 2026-10-26). A duplicate key fails it with 2627. All string columns, the key columns included, are compared as bytes. So a change only in case or trailing spaces is landed as an update in place; for a key column that update rewrites the key in place. Restoring a soft-deleted row counts as an update. A row that is already soft-deleted and still missing from the source is not touched and not counted. The live row count is checked against the source count (RULE-005).
dim_payer_type is not seeded. Like dim_payment_method, it stays empty until usp_load_dim_payer_type runs: by hand until MOD-016's run sequence calls it. The load never deletes from the dimension, and load_id holds the etl_run_log.log_id of the load. No grants are needed by this module.

Test-first: the first run had 0 of 23 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 23 of 23 and 7 unit test(s), in 3 run(s).
